$comment: Eval categories: one per main-chat task class, plus tricky groups. 'cover' says what the 8-10 cases must span. Cases are written fresh and anonymized; real prompts only teach their shape.

mechanical.cover: translate, reformat, convert units/format, split or shorten given text, rename in given text, fix punctuation; EN and RU; short and long inputs

explore.cover: web lookups (weather, prices, scores, release versions, opening hours), find a file or symbol, list things in a repo, read logs, summarize a short file; questions and commands

brainstorm.cover: titles, hooks, angles, names, episode ideas, taglines; creative and product contexts

scoped-code.cover: small well-specified code changes: fix a named bug, rename across a module, add a flag, implement a small spec'd function, typo in code

docs.cover: everyday docs, README edits, slide outlines, spreadsheets, meeting notes, internal how-tos

image-prompt.cover: prompts and settings for local image or video generation (ComfyUI-style workflows, LoRA, ControlNet, negative prompts), editing such prompts

engineering.cover: everyday multi-file engineering: features across modules, integration work, refactors of moderate size, performance fixes, working through a spec

vision.cover: look at a screenshot or image, compare two renders, check a UI against a mockup, drive a browser or desktop app

final-copy.cover: words the audience reads or hears: social posts, video voice-over scripts, landing page copy, newsletters, final episode scripts; EN and RU

structure.cover: episode arcs, beat sheets, long-form outlines, chapter structure, course outlines, cross-section consistency of a long document

critique.cover: judge creative or visual work: review a script, critique an image set, QC a deck, judge which of several drafts is best; not code review

brand-visual.cover: brand-book pages, logo usage, scene and composition direction, key visuals, visual identity decisions

architecture.cover: system design, ADRs, technical plans, data model design, cross-module boundaries, choosing between technologies

rare-hard.cover: migrations, major rewrites, deep multi-source research, leading many subagents on a long job

learn-explain.cover: explain a concept, how a library works, difference between two approaches, teach me X; no changes requested

data-analysis.cover: analyze a CSV or spreadsheet, compute metrics, write SQL, find trends in numbers, build a chart from data

test-writing.cover: write unit or integration tests for existing code, raise coverage, add a regression test for a described bug

devops-config.cover: CI pipelines, Dockerfiles, deploy scripts, env config, package manager and tool setup, scheduled jobs

long-read.cover: read a long transcript, report, PDF, chat export or log and pull out decisions, risks or a summary

debugging.cover: find why something fails, crashes, hangs or gives wrong output; stack traces, flaky tests, works-on-my-machine

code-review.cover: review a PR, diff, branch or commit for bugs, security and missing cases

math.cover: proofs, probability, statistics questions, derivations, quantitative estimates with reasoning

security-review.cover: security review of code or config, threat model, injection and auth risks, secrets handling

follow-up.cover: short continuations after a prior task ('ok do it', 'and the tests too', 'make it shorter', 'давай'); each case gives the prior task in history; the needed tier is the prior task's

russian.cover: tasks written in Russian or mixed Russian/English across dev and creative work, from trivial to hard

very-short.cover: prompts under 25 characters that are new tasks or chat: 'hi', 'thanks', 'what time is it in Tokyo', 'run the tests', 'deploy'

mixed-task.cover: one prompt with two kinds of work ('find the bug and fix it', 'research X then write the post'); the needed tier is the harder part's

misleading-words.cover: trigger words in the wrong sense: 'review my outline' (creative), 'translate the architecture diagram into a checklist', 'find a better word', 'test this headline'

project-specific.cover: the same words meaning different things per project type (webapp, studio, brand); each case names its project; use project keywords from evals/projects

explicit-ask.cover: the prompt names a model or effort ('use haiku for this', 'think hard', 'do it with opus', 'на sonnet', 'from now on use sonnet', 'low effort'); the needed tier is exactly what was asked

general-chat.cover: greetings, thanks, meta questions about the assistant, small talk, quick opinions
